div.p: SCRA runs a full calendar of nets, classes, exam sessions, public service events, and the annual Field Day / Winter Field Day gatherings. The pages below cover what each one is about; for the live, up-to-date calendar of specific dates, use Odoo's own Events app once it's populated rather than this static page.

SCRA's weekend Technician License course has trained over 250 people since 2007, with an emphasis on practical knowledge over rote memorization - the goal is knowledgeable ham radio operators, not just licensees.
The program spans three days:
Location details are provided to registered students.
The course itself is free, taught entirely by volunteers. Two fees apply when obtaining a licence:

ul.li: $15 Volunteer Examiner testing fee ($5 for minors)
$35 FCC licensing fee, due only after passing the exam

div.p: The exam consists of 35 multiple-choice questions covering electronics theory, antennas, radio etiquette, safety, and regulations. Passing requires correctly answering at least 26 questions. The FCC issues a 10-year licence on success.

SCRA recommends the "Gordon West Technician Class Study Guide, 2022-2026 edition" (~$30) for exam preparation. Students who study beforehand have a much better chance of passing, and nearly all students pass on their first attempt.
Handheld VHF radios for local communication can cost as little as $50, while HF equipment for long-distance communication typically runs around $400 used.
Register in advance by emailing Kathy KM6URP at education@sonomacountyradioamateurs.com.
Club members can get one-on-one mentoring to upgrade to General Class or Amateur Extra Class - same contact as above.
SCRA's mentorship program pairs new licensees with experienced operators, opening the door to satellite communication, emergency services, contests, and equipment building.

SCRA administers amateur radio licence exams using the ExamTools web application. Candidates may take exams electronically on their own device, or on paper.

p.em: Specific upcoming session dates are time-bound content, not carried over here - re-enter current sessions via Odoo's own Events app rather than treating this as a static page. Pre-registration (optional) is available through hamstudy.org.

div.p: FCC Registration Number (FRN): all applicants for new licences must obtain an FRN directly from the FCC prior to the exam session, at fcc.gov/uls. Exams are held on weekends, and the FCC's website has occasionally been down on weekends, so don't leave this to the last minute.

Pre-Exam Registration: register at hamstudy.org by clicking "Find a Session" and locating "Sonoma County Radio Amateurs VE Team." You'll need either your FRN (new applicants) or your current callsign (upgrades).

ul.li: One photo ID, or two non-photo IDs
Exam fee: $15 for adults (18+) or $5 for minors - cash or check only, payable to "ARRL-VEC" (no cards or electronic payment)
A #2 pencil and eraser for a paper exam, or a laptop/ tablet/smartphone with internet for an electronic exam
Original and photocopy of your current amateur radio licence, if upgrading
Original and photocopy of any valid CSCEs, if applicable

div.p: Calculators may be used if all memory and programs are erased; cell phone calculator functions are prohibited.

The ARRL-VEC charges exam administration fees as above. The FCC separately charges a $35 application fee, not payable at the exam - after passing, the FCC emails payment instructions with a 10-day deadline. Minors may be eligible for reimbursement through the ARRL Youth Licensing Grant Program.
Bring your signed original licence and a photocopy.
Holders of expired General, Advanced, or Amateur Extra licences may qualify for partial credit toward retesting, though at minimum they must still pass the current 35-question Technician exam.
For those unable to attend in person, PARC offers online exam options - see parcradio.org.

SCRA provides radio communication support for regional events held in areas with limited cellular coverage, and welcomes all amateur radio operators - particularly those new to the hobby - to participate.

Newcomers can join as "Shadows" to learn portable radio operations from experienced hams while exploring Sonoma County. SCRA maintains four portable radio kits available for loan to operators without their own equipment.

For bike events, amateur radio operators can fill support vehicle (SAG - Support And Gear) positions. Event organizers, not SCRA, manage SAG driver recruitment - volunteer through the event organizer's own website and identify yourself as a licensed operator.

SCRA provides communications for numerous cycling events including Climate Ride Wine Country, Fish Rock, Levi's Gran Fondo, Lake Sonoma Relentless, Giro Bello, Terrible Two, Bike Monkey, Wine Country Century, Bike MS, and Tour de Cure.

div.p: The ARRL established Field Day in the 1930s to test amateur radio operators' emergency communication capabilities. Over time it has evolved into one of the hobby's most beloved events, extending beyond emergency preparedness to celebrate amateur radio more broadly. Field Day offers hands-on experience with station setup, antenna installation, contest operation, logging, and community interaction. See the ARRL Field Day website for more.
SCRA's Field Day runs at Youth Community Park, 1750 Fulton Rd, Santa Rosa (across from Piner High School).
SCRA typically runs five operational stations:
The GOTA station welcomes unlicensed individuals and those without a General-class licence. Participants can make contacts under the supervision of a licensed General-class operator.
Field Day needs volunteers across setup, operating, food, and teardown - contact the Field Day Chairman to get involved:

div.p: SCRA runs Winter Field Day each January at Sugarloaf Ridge State Park, at the group campsite adjacent to the Robert Ferguson Observatory.
SCRA typically runs five stations: Phone, CW, Digital, Satellite, and GOTA (Get-On-The-Air, for newer/unlicensed operators, with an educational/mentorship focus).

Points are calculated as: (QSO count) x (power output multiplier) x (band/mode multiplier). Phone contacts earn 1 point; CW and digital modes earn 2 points. QRP stations (under 5W CW / 10W phone) receive a 2x multiplier, others 1x. Each band/mode combination adds 1 to the multiplier.
Coffee, donuts, and a Saturday pizza dinner are typically provided. Parking is limited on-site, so carpooling is encouraged.
